content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in West Palm Beach

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a four-year degree with three years of project-management experience, or a high-school diploma with five years of experience. Document your project leadership history and verify you meet PMI's formal education requirement before proceeding with your application.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend all 35 required contact hours from anywhere in West Palm Beach on a schedule that fits your work commitments. Our active certified practitioners deliver real-world case studies and exam-aligned content throughout.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, submit your PMI application directly to the Project Management Institute. Include your project-experience documentation and pay PMI's examination fee. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before booking your exam date.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, practice tests, and instructor guidance to reinforce critical concepts. Schedule your exam with Pearson Vue at a testing center or via proctored online delivery. Our team remains available to answer final questions before you sit for the assessment.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) over a three-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. Pursue continuing education through project-management courses, conferences, or volunteer work. PMI requires ongoing commitment to professional growth in order to renew.
